How College Students Use Gemini: Features and Study Methods

2026-10-27 · GlobalTech Daily Editorial Desk · Source: blog.google

Introduction and Key Takeaways

According to an official blog post by Google featuring insights from 15 Google Student Ambassadors and students across various universities, college students utilize Gemini for studying, organizing notes, managing projects, and mastering course materials. Key takeaways from the report show that students leverage Gemini features such as study notebooks, Gemini Live, Guided Learning, custom quizzes, Audio Overviews, Nano Banana, Gemini in Chrome, Deep Research, and app integrations to enhance learning and productivity.

Study Notebooks, Guided Learning, and Quizzes

Students use study notebooks to turn course materials into personalized, bite-sized lessons. Beverlyn T. from the University of Southern California notes they make studying manageable before finals, while Nina R. from the University of California, Santa Barbara highlights how they refresh memories on 50-page papers and compare competing viewpoints. For practice, students create custom quizzes. Shuang P. from New York University states that practice quizzes build confidence for high-stakes tests, and Tobi U. from the University of California, Riverside uses them to check work and understand question logic when answer keys are absent. Additionally, Guided Learning helps build understanding rather than providing direct answers. Fehmaan K. from George Mason University explains that pasting work and letting Gemini walk through mistakes via open-ended questions helps catch errors effectively.

Gemini Live, Audio Overviews, and Image Generation

Gemini Live enables voice and camera interactions. Skylar E. from San Diego State University uses it for practicing interviews and presentations, and Debbie C. from The University of Texas, Austin uses the camera feature to receive step-by-step assistance with design tools. For audio learning, students like Nina R. and Parikshit M. from Rutgers University use Audio Overviews to convert documents and conflicting articles into podcast-style conversations for review while walking across campus. Furthermore, Nelson G. from Morehouse College uses the image generator Nano Banana to visualize ideas and format images, while Beverlyn T. uses it to design club flyers and social media posts.

Browser Assistance, Deep Research, and App Integrations

Gemini in Chrome assists users directly in the browser. Megan J. from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign uses it to efficiently review wrong answers without copying and pasting, and Fehmaan K. uses it to decipher complex documents. For extensive projects, Deep Research automatically browses websites and creates multi-page reports. Annitha K. from San Diego State University notes it saves time by compiling exhaustive market analyses and literature reviews. Finally, students connect Gemini to apps like Google Drive, Google Calendar, Gmail, and Google Sheets. Skylar E. has Gemini reference syllabi to organize assignments in Calendar, Aaryaman B. from Michigan State University uses Sheets for task tracking, and Megan J. manages teaching assistant emails to prevent messages from getting lost.
